title: Public Auditability (Verifiable Transparency of State-Affecting Actions)

dascp.note: Establishes the public-verifiability content of an audit trail (every consequential action carries a publicly checkable record); does not bind the trail to synchronized timestamps or external-activity inclusion that C32-R additionally requires.
Auditability is a precondition for meaningful data lineage: lineage records are only useful if independently checkable, which is what public-auditability provides.

descriptions.semantic: Every state-affecting action of consequence is accompanied by a publicly available, independently verifiable record sufficient for any party to reconstruct or check that the action conformed to policy — without relying on a trusted insider. Auditability is the precondition for trustless verification, dispute resolution, and accountability.
descriptions.system_theoretic: An observability constraint on the LTS: each consequential transition emits an externally checkable witness (event, commitment, or proof) such that an external monitor can decide policy conformance from the public trace alone.
descriptions.security: Underpins trust-minimization: solvency claims, governance legitimacy, and bridge correctness are only meaningful if independently checkable. The tension with privacy (BPO:0003) is real and is resolved NOT by weakening either, but by selective disclosure — publishing commitments plus zero-knowledge proofs that the hidden data satisfies the audited policy.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Realized through events/logs, on-chain commitments (Merkle roots, polynomial commitments), and verifiable proofs. Failure modes: consequential state changes with no emitted record, off-chain-only data with no on-chain commitment, or 'audit' that requires trusting the operator's API.
descriptions.formal_verification: Checkable as a safety/observability obligation: prove that every consequential transition emits a record from which an external verifier can decide conformance. Combined with ZK, the obligation becomes 'emits a sound proof of conformance' (delegating to BPO:0070).

formalization.signature: Consequential ⊆ Op; record(o): the public witness emitted by o; Verify_ext(record, policy) ∈ {0,1} computable by any external party.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Auditability:  ∀ s,s',o . ( o ∈ Consequential ∧ s --[o]--> s' ) → ( emits(o, r) ∧ ( Verify_ext(r, policy) = 1 ↔ conformant(o) ) ).
With privacy:  r is a commitment c plus a proof π s.t. KnowledgeSound(π) (BPO:0070) attests conformant(o) without revealing the secret witness (BPO:0003).

hoare.post: an externally verifiable record of o's policy-conformance is public

formalization.state_machine: Each consequential edge is annotated with an emitted observable; the property is that the public projection of the trace is sufficient to decide conformance.
formalization.type_theoretic: Declassification policy: auditability is a controlled-release obligation — exactly the policy-relevant predicate is made Low-observable (possibly via a proof), the rest may remain High (private).

relationships.note: Full transparency and full witness-privacy are in direct tension on the same data; selective disclosure (commitment + ZK proof) is the standard reconciliation.
Auditing a ZK-mediated action relies on the proof being knowledge-sound.

attack_surface.pattern: a consequential mutation emits no event/commitment; external parties cannot detect or verify it
attack_surface.notes: Mandate events/commitments on all consequential ops.

attack_surface.pattern: critical data lives off-chain with no on-chain commitment; 'audit' reduces to trusting an API
attack_surface.notes: Commit roots on-chain; publish data availability.

attack_surface.pattern: proof-of-reserves snapshot that omits liabilities or double-counts
attack_surface.notes: Audit must bind BOTH assets and liabilities (cross-ref BPO:0101).

events: domain events for every consequential action
metrics: fraction of consequential ops with verifiable records
invariant_checkpoints: no consequential selector lacks an emitted record

strategies.notes: Prove every consequential transition emits its record.
Independently recompute conformance from the public trace.

testability: every consequential action produces a record an external party can verify

runtime: on-chain proof verification for private actions
design_patterns: bind assets AND liabilities in reserve proofs

assumptions.statement: Published data / commitments are actually available (data availability holds).

provenance.notes: Exists to host the privacy↔transparency tension and demonstrate reconciliation by selective disclosure rather than weakening either property.
